title: More Than $1.3 Million in FEMA Funding for CUC Emergency Generator Support
text: The Commonwealth Utilities Corporation (CUC) has received $1,308,655.88 in federal funding to support emergency generator operations following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. This includes $1,059,132.68 for emergency protective measures and an additional $249,523.20 to fund the use of temporary generators to help maintain essential services and reduce immediate threats to public health, safety, and property. Both awards are funded at 100% by FEMA under Section 403 of the Stafford Act, with no local cost share required. Reliable power is critical to our communities, especially in the aftermath of a disaster, and this assistance helps CUC respond to urgent needs while supporting the Commonwealth’s recovery.

title: Responding to the Suspension of EVS-TAP
text: Last week, the Department of Homeland Security announced the suspension of the CNMI Economic Vitality and Security Travel Authorization Program (EVS-TAP), adding another challenge to an already struggling tourism industry. With visitor arrivals declining and our businesses and families facing increasing economic pressure, the consequences of a prolonged suspension could be significant. Immediately following the announcement, I spoke directly with the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, and House leadership about the suspension and the urgency of restoring the program. Secretary Mullin personally assured me that he would work with the CNMI to understand and address the concerns that led to the decision. I also wrote to President Trump requesting his personal intervention and an expedited review involving DHS, the Department of the Interior, and the Commonwealth government. EVS-TAP was established during his first administration, and I believe there is a path to resolving the outstanding concerns and restoring the program. Already, I have spoken with senior leaders in both the administration and Congress about the critical condition of the CNMI economy and the role the federal government has in preventing its collapse. Our tourism industry, government revenues, and the livelihoods of our people are all connected, and federal decisions affecting our economy must take those consequences seriously. EVS-TAP remains suspended, and there are procedures for addressing the security and law enforcement concerns that may arise under the program. My immediate priority is working with our federal partners to resolve the outstanding issues and secure its resumption as quickly as possible. There is a great deal at stake for our Commonwealth, and I will continue pressing for the urgency our situation demands.

title: Rota Mayor’s Office Receives $320,000 in FEMA Funding for Equipment
text: Rota’s recovery efforts continue with $320,680 in FEMA funding approved for the Rota Mayor’s Office to purchase equipment under an alternate project following Typhoon Mawar. This $427,574 project is funded through FEMA’s Public Assistance Program under Section 406 of the Stafford Act, with the federal government covering 75% of the cost. This investment will help strengthen the Mayor’s Office’s resources and support its ability to serve the people of Rota.

title: Supporting Higher Education and Workforce Development
text: On Tuesday, we welcomed Northern Marianas College Interim President Frankie Eliptico and members of the State Higher Education Executive Officers Association (SHEEO), Christen Whitfield, Rob Andersen, and Tom Harnisch, to the Saipan district office. SHEEO advocates for state-level leadership in higher education policy and connects state higher education systems with the federal government. The organization has represented NMC’s interests for more than a decade. NMC was recently selected as one of only eight institutions nationwide to receive a highly competitive grant to help implement Workforce Pell programs, expanding opportunities for students to gain skills for in-demand careers. Congratulations to President Eliptico for your outstanding leadership and to the entire NMC team for your dedication to strengthening higher education opportunities and creating pathways to success for students across the Marianas.

title: VCU Students Study the CNMI’s Resilience and Recovery
text:
Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU), through its Institute for Sustainable Energy and Environment, brought students to Saipan, Tinian, and Guam to study how territorial governance, disaster recovery, and environmental challenges affect island communities. Working alongside students from the University of Guam, they explored issues ranging from typhoon recovery and clean energy to food security and deep-sea mining, with the goal of better understanding these challenges and informing future solutions. Having grown up in the CNMI, I know our islands are more than just a place on the map. They are home to resilient people who continue to rebuild after devastating storms, including Super Typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi. We’re glad to see these students come to Saipan and Tinian to listen to our people and see firsthand the realities our communities face. We hope their research brings greater attention to the CNMI’s needs and reminds more Americans that our islands have valuable lessons to share with the rest of our nation.

title: Working with Navy Leadership on the CNMI’s Economic and Infrastructure Needs
text: The economic challenges facing our Commonwealth have become increasingly urgent, and I have been working to make sure our federal partners understand what is at stake for our people and for the United States' long-term presence in the Pacific. On Tuesday, I met with Admiral Mietus to discuss the worsening economic conditions in the CNMI, including the impact of declining tourism, rising utility costs, and the recent suspension of EVS-TAP. We talked about the need for a coordinated federal response and the importance of recognizing that a strong local economy is essential to supporting our nation's defense interests in the Marianas. The following day, we continued those conversations with Admiral Mietus and Andy Weedon, Director of Policy and Strategy for the Secretary of the Navy, alongside Governor Apatang. Our discussions focused on infrastructure investments that could benefit both our communities and the military, including improvements to our power systems, airports, and harbors on Saipan, Tinian, and Rota. We also discussed opportunities to move priority projects forward through federal infrastructure programs and the importance of keeping our agencies working together to turn these discussions into actual investments. I appreciate Admiral Mietus and Director Weedon taking the time to engage with us on these issues and see the challenges facing our islands firsthand. There is a great deal of work ahead, and I look forward to continuing these conversations as we pursue the federal support and investments our Commonwealth needs.

title: Lofgren Secures Over $54 Million for Pajaro River Flood Protection As El Niño Is Expected to Strengthen
text:
WATSONVILLE, CA — Today, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) delivered a $54,830,000 check for the Pajaro River Flood Risk Management Project, one of her 13 community projects she submitted for the Fiscal Year 2026 congressional appropriations cycle. This is the largest single community project that Lofgren secured this year, which is being completed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) San Francisco District, in partnership with the Pajaro Regional Flood Management Agency (PRFMA). Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) also requested congressional funding for this project.

“With El Niño expected to intensify in the early months of 2027, it’s critical that the residents and businesses along the Pajaro River have necessary flood protection,” said Rep. Lofgren. “Last year, I was proud to announce nearly $40 million for levee and floodwall construction in Watsonville, and I’m proud to have submitted this additional $54 million as one of my community projects this year. That’s going to help save lives and property, and I’m proud to have worked with Senators Padilla and Schiff to prioritize this project funding.”

“Consistent funding for the Pajaro River flood control project is critically important, and we are grateful to Rep. Lofgren for her work to keep the project moving forward and fulfilling our commitments to the vulnerable residents and businesses in the Pajaro Valley,” said Mark Strudley, Executive Director of PRFMA.

“Future improvements to the levee will make a real difference in reducing flood risks and protecting the people who call Watsonville and the Pajaro Valley home,” said Watsonville City Manager Tamara Vides. This is an investment in the safety, stability, and future of our community. We are thankful for the advocacy and support provided by Congresswoman Lofgren.”

The residents and businesses of Watsonville and Pajaro have been waiting for 50 years for flood protection and during that time have suffered significant damage and loss of life due to weather events. On March 11, 2023, a serious levee failure resulted in the evacuation of more than 2,000 people in the Town of Pajaro, 200 water rescues, significant flooding of farms, and closure of Highway 1. The farms impacted by flooding are vital contributors to the regional agricultural industry, where none of the fruit and vegetable crops are federally subsidized and floods can result in the loss of 2-3 growing seasons.

According to the National Weather Service, El Niño continues to strengthen with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027. Lofgren has urged Californians to prepare for storm season and sign up for emergency alerts. Tips and resources for El Niño can be viewed on her website.

title: Rep. Miller Announced $4.5 Million for Rural Water Infrastructure Expansion Benefiting Seven Illinois Counties
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Mary Miller (IL-15) announced $4.5 million in federal funding to support the expansion of EJ Water Cooperative’s Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant. The investment will double the facility’s treatment capacity, strengthening access to reliable water service for families, farmers, and businesses across seven Central Illinois counties: Shelby, Effingham, Montgomery, Fayette, Cumberland, Christian, and Clay.

“Our farmers, small businesses, and rural communities are the backbone of America, and they deserve the infrastructure necessary to thrive. I’m proud to have secured $4.5 million to support this critical expansion in Illinois’ 15th District,” said Congresswoman Mary Miller. “This investment will meet growing demand and strengthen the essential infrastructure that families and businesses across our rural communities will depend on for generations.”

Background:

Founded in 1989, EJ Water Cooperative is the largest rural water cooperative in Illinois, serving a rural population of more than 48,000 residents. The Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant was constructed in 2010 near Beecher City and serves EJ Water’s fastest-growing western service area.

As demand continues to increase, EJ Water has expanded its infrastructure to support rural communities, including the construction of a 250-million-gallon reservoir in 2023. The cooperative also works with smaller municipalities facing aging or inadequate water treatment facilities, helping provide dependable, affordable water service to underserved communities throughout Central Illinois.

title: The 119th Congress did more by making government do less
text:
WASHINGTON— House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) published an op-ed in The Hill on how House Republicans used the 119th Congress to shrink Washington’s reach and return more freedom to the American people.

“I don’t call the 119th Congress the most successful because of the paper it produced.” Chairwoman McClain said. “I say it because we changed the direction of the country. Washington has enough monuments to what government can build. We spent this Congress creating room for what Americans can build instead.”

Read the full piece below:

— —

Washington has a peculiar definition of progress. A new program is an accomplishment. A new regulation is action. A new federal office means somebody is finally doing something. That is why some of the most important work Republicans did this Congress involved undoing that so-called “progress.”

For decades, Washington accumulated authority one seemingly reasonable decision at a time. Congress delegated power to an agency full of faceless bureaucrats. The agency wrote a rule. The rule became another permit to obtain, expense to absorb, or decision somebody in Washington had already made for you.

Government grows quietly that way. Freedom disappears just as quietly. House Republicans of the 119th Congress came to Washington with the idea that the most consequential thing government can do is return freedom to the American people. Yes, we passed over 900 pieces of legislation this Congress, the second most in U.S. history, but that matters much less than what changed once the votes were cast.

House Republicans have overturned 23 federal rules through the Congressional Review Act, the most in history and more successful repeals than every previous Congress combined. In one session, we have turned a little-used oversight law into one of Washington’s most powerful tools for permanently returning authority from federal regulators to the people they regulate.

Washington is accustomed to ratchets that turn in one direction. Government expands, the bureaucracy adjusts, and everyone learns to live with the new baseline. We turned the ratchet backward.

Democrats would have let the 2017 tax cuts expire and taken more money out of Americans’ pockets. We made them permanent, cut taxes on tips and overtime, delivered new relief for seniors, and restored incentives to invest and build in America.

Americans have already claimed more than $82 billion in individual tax relief. Over the decade, the tax changes we enacted are projected to give $4.6 trillion back to families and businesses, and the laws enacted cut projected federal spending by roughly $1.1 trillion, meaning Washington will take less of Americans’ money.

People take bigger chances when they know more of the reward will still belong to them. That is how opportunity compounds and how countries grow. But opportunity can only flourish where freedom is protected by order and the rules still mean something.

A limited government is not a weak government. It does a smaller number of things, and it does the essential ones well. It must defend the country, enforce the law, protect basic rights, and establish rules that allow a free society to function.

Securing a nation’s borders is among the most basic responsibilities that government has. Democrats chose to dismantle our border and turn lawlessness into policy. Republicans flipped the script and have not allowed a single illegal immigrant to be released into the country in 16 months.

This Congress put the philosophy of limited government into practice across the economy. We gave small businesses tax certainty to hire and invest. We cleared regulatory barriers so manufacturers can expand, unleashed more American energy, and made it easier to build. None of these policies determines what Americans must do with their lives. They expand what Americans are free to do for themselves.

The alternative is government by permission slip. Washington chooses which industries deserve to grow, which products people may buy, which energy sources are acceptable, and how much of a worker’s success belongs to somebody else. There needs to be a line between the power government is granted by the people, and the freedom Americans deserve to keep.

That is the foundation the 119th Congress has spent two years laying.

A foundation is not glamorous. Nobody walks through a finished house admiring the concrete underneath it, but everything built above depends on whether the foundation is strong.

Tax certainty. Regulatory relief. A secure border. American energy. Lower crime. More room to work, build and invest. These are not the finished house. They are what makes everything that comes next possible.

I don’t call the 119th Congress the most successful because of the paper it produced. I say it because we changed the direction of the country. Washington has enough monuments to what government can build. We spent this Congress creating room for what Americans can build instead.

The government does not know what your life should look like. Neither do I, and that’s precisely the point — you do.

title: Congressman Menefee Joins the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Representative Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) has joined the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC) as an Associate Member, bringing the Caucus to a historic 86 Members of the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate, its largest membership since its founding.

“Houston is one of the most diverse cities in the nation. The strength and resilience of our many cultures, including our Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities, are woven into the fabric of our district. I’m proud to join the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus. More than 40,000 AANHPI residents call TX-18 home, and I’m committed to making sure our community has a seat at the table. Thank you to Chair Meng for the warm welcome. I look forward to being an ally in this fight,” said Rep. Christian D. Menefee.

“I am thrilled to welcome Congressman Christian Menefee as CAPAC’s new Associate Member,” said Rep. Grace Meng, Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus. “We need allies in Congress who are committed to fighting for the needs of Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders across the country—including right in the heart of Houston. title: Rep. Obernolte Demands Answers on Medi-Cal Oversight
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23) led members of the California delegation in sending a letter to California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Director Michelle Baass expressing concerns over the department's oversight of the Medi-Cal program following a recent report from the California State Auditor identifying deficiencies in its efforts to investigate potentially improper billing and recover overpayments.

The letter, signed by Representatives Ken Calvert (CA-41), Tom McClintock (CA-05), David Valadao (CA-22), Young Kim (CA-40), Vince Fong (CA-20), and James Gallagher (CA-01), requests information on the department's efforts to strengthen program oversight, address potentially fraudulent billing, and safeguard taxpayer dollars.

According to the October 15 audit, DHCS identified approximately 28,000 Medi-Cal providers as high risk for potentially improper billing during fiscal year 2024–2025, but had not initiated referrals or investigations for more than 26,000 of them. These providers collectively accounted for at least $12 billion in Medi-Cal services during that period.

The audit also found that DHCS identified more than $2 billion in provider overpayments between fiscal years 2020 and 2025, approximately $300 million of which remain unrecovered.

The findings come amid additional federal scrutiny of California's Medi-Cal program. On October 20, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced it would defer an additional $1.2 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California over concerns regarding documentation supporting certain Medi-Cal expenditures.

“Medi-Cal provides critical care to millions of Californians, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that is not available to help our most vulnerable citizens access the care they need,” said Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23). “The California State Auditor's findings raise serious concerns about the state's oversight of this program, particularly the failure to investigate more than 26,000 providers identified as high risk for potentially improper billing. California taxpayers deserve to know that their money is being used wisely and appropriately. Stronger oversight is necessary to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting the patients who depend on this critical program.”

“It’s critical that California take every measure possible to eliminate fraud in the Medi-Cal program. We owe it taxpayers to verify payments to Medi-Cal providers and ensure all of our resources are being dedicated to the actual health care needs of Californians,” said Congressman Ken Calvert (CA-41).

“California’s Medi-Cal program is a critical lifeline for our most vulnerable, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that can’t go toward helping those in need,” said Congressman David Valadao (CA-22). “The California Department of Health Care Services has a responsibility to properly investigate fraudulent billing and improper payments, and I urge the agency to take immediate action to strengthen program oversight, hold bad actors accountable, and ensure taxpayer funds are being used appropriately.”

“Medi-Cal is supposed to be a lifeline for California’s most vulnerable, not an opportunity for fraudsters to cash in at taxpayers’ expense,” said Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40). “The fact that California failed to investigate thousands of providers flagged for potential fraud, despite those providers accounting for $12 billion in claims, raises serious questions about the state’s oversight efforts. Every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that could have gone toward caring for seniors, mothers, and children who depend on the services Medi-Cal provides. Californians deserve answers, accountability, and assurance that their tax dollars are going where they’re needed most.”

“Medi-Cal exists to protect our most vulnerable neighbors, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar taken from the patients and families who depend on it,” said Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20). "$12 billion in potentially improper payments is a failure of basic oversight, and patients are the ones who pay the price for California’s mismanagement. Sacramento owes Californians real answers and immediate action to protect Medi-Cal for those who need it, and to keep it fiscally solvent for future generations.”

“California taxpayers are pouring billions of dollars into Medi-Cal, and they deserve to know that money is being spent responsibly—not lost to fraud, waste, and bad oversight," said Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01). "The State Auditor’s findings raise serious questions about why thousands of high-risk providers went without further investigation and why hundreds of millions of dollars in overpayments remain unrecovered. We cannot afford to ignore these warning signs. Period. Medi-Cal must protect the vulnerable Californians who depend on it, and that starts with holding the system accountable, rooting out fraud, and ensuring taxpayer dollars go toward legitimate patient care.”

title: Rep. Panetta Announces Over $3.8 Million for Santa Cruz  Fire Department Medical Response Vehicle Pilot Program
text:
Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) announced $3,837,779 in federal funding for the Santa Cruz Fire Department to test a faster, more targeted response to medical emergencies, including traffic crashes. The funding comes from the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant program, which helps improve roadway safety by investing in safety strategies to reduce serious traffic injuries and fatalities.

The project combines two tools to help improve emergency response on Santa Cruz roadways. It will test a cloud-based system that gives emergency vehicles priority at traffic signals, connected to the dispatch system, as well as a smaller medical response vehicle for calls that do not involve a fire, including traffic crashes. The City of Santa Cruz will evaluate whether these tools improve response times and care after crashes, particularly along roads with high rates of serious injuries and key routes to hospitals.

“Every second counts for first responders when it comes to driving on our local roads and highways,” said Rep. Panetta. “This federal investment will allow the city of Santa Cruz to test potentially lifesaving technology to help emergency vehicles reach people more quickly and first responders provide timely, effective care. I’m proud to ensure that the federal government plays its part to help our local first responders do their job for the safety of communities in California’s 19th Congressional District.”

“This grant will allow Santa Cruz to explore new ways to help first responders reach injured patients faster, provide lifesaving care, and improve roadway safety,” said Santa Cruz Mayor Fred Keeley. “I am grateful for Congressman Panetta’s support in delivering this significant federal investment to strengthen emergency response and make our community safer.”

“Keeping our community safe is one of our most important responsibilities, and this investment gives Santa Cruz an exciting opportunity to strengthen how we respond to emergencies. We’re grateful to Congressman Panetta for securing this funding and recognizing the importance of investing in innovative solutions that can help save lives and make our streets safer for everyone. We’re excited to test these tools, evaluate their effectiveness, and identify opportunities to improve service to our community,” said Santa Cruz City Manager Matt Huffaker.

The SS4A grant program was established by the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act in 2021. Since the program’s inception, the cities of Santa Cruz, Monterey, Paso Robles, and San Jose, together with Santa Cruz County, Santa Clara County, the Transportation Agency for Monterey County, and the San Luis Obispo Council of Governments, have received more than $28.7 million through the SS4A program.

Rep. Panetta has previously secured federal investments for a new fire engine in Santa Cruz, pedestrian safety and lighting improvements along Bay Avenue in Capitola, and road safety improvements along Highways 9 and 236 in Boulder Creek.

title: From Texas Scorecard: Chip Roy Seeks DOJ Review of Allegations Surrounding Travis County DA’s Refusal To Prosecute Afghan National
text:
The below story appeared in the Texas Scorecard:

U.S. Reps. Chip Roy and Josh Brecheen are seeking records from the U.S. Department of Justice and an investigation into whistleblower allegations involving Travis County District Attorney José Garza’s decision not to prosecute an Afghan national accused of felony solicitation of prostitution.

The lawmakers’ letter cites a September 14 whistleblower complaint from Major Joshua Mast concerning Afghan national Aminullah Amin. According to the lawmakers, Garza’s office declined to prosecute the solicitation charges on July 22, citing the “interest of justice.”

Amin is embroiled in a custody dispute with Mast and his wife over a seven-year-old girl.

“The complaint raises the question whether the charging decision may have been improperly influenced so that the accused in that case could continue his custody pursuit of [the] seven-year-old little girl in our nation’s highest court,” the congressmen wrote.

The custody dispute began after an Afghan baby was found in the rubble of a rural compound raided by U.S. Army Rangers.

The State Department helped place her with an Afghan couple identified as relatives, who raised her for 18 months while Joshua Mast and his wife obtained a Virginia adoption order without notifying them.

After helping the Afghan family evacuate to the United States in 2021, Mast took custody of the girl. Lower Virginia courts ruled in the Afghan couple’s favor, but the state’s highest court sided with the Masts, citing a six-month statutory deadline for challenging the adoption.

The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear the Afghan couple’s appeal earlier this month.

Roy (R–Austin) and Brecheen (R–OK) also request a review of evidence from two 2021 forensic extractions of phones used by Amin. The lawmakers say Mast’s complaint identifies potential investigative leads involving national security and immigration screening.

“The Complaint identifies leads involving alleged Taliban contacts, possible al-Qaeda connections, and eleven distinct SIM-card identifiers associated with one of the phones,” they wrote.

This letter follows a June committee inquiry into Garza’s immigration-related policies.

Roy, along with U.S. Reps. Jim Jordan (R–OH) and Tom McClintock (R–CA), wrote to Garza earlier this year “concerning his office’s immigration-related policies and their consequences for public safety and the rule of law.”

“Under your leadership, the Travis County District Attorney’s Office has routinely undermined the rule of law under the guise of safeguarding the public,” the congressmen wrote. “You previously committed to ‘[p]rotect immigrant communities’ by ‘creat[ing] a [district attorney’s] office that considers the impact of charges and convictions’ on foreign nationals and ‘ensures that the sentence imposed is not unduly harsh for any class of people.’”

Roy and Brecheen raised concerns that Garza is continuing a “soft-on-crime” approach that could also threaten national security.

“Shielding criminal aliens from immigration enforcement in Travis County or elsewhere undermines public safety and impedes enforcement of federal law,” Roy and Brecheen wrote.

“Above all, unresolved questions about potential terrorism connections involving a foreign national arrested for an apparent felony and pursuing custody of a child in American courts demand prompt examination.”

Garza has not responded to a request for comment regarding Roy and Brecheen’s accusations against him.

title: Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District
text:
Tualatin, OR — Today, Congresswomen Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), alongside Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced they secured the release of over $530,000 in federal funding from the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) to support Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District (TSWCD).

In 2022, TSWCD applied to the NRCS for funding to improve fish habitat in Washington County. This work included replacing deteriorated culverts with bridges and modern culverts that help threatened species like steelhead trout move through local waterways. In February 2024, NRCS approved and obligated $1,074,887 to reimburse TSWCD for their work.

As of early September 2026, NRCS had only paid $543,837 of the over $1.07 million they had promised to TSWCD. This $531,000 shortfall has severely challenged TSWCD’s budget and would have stuck the taxpayers of Washington County with the bill. Following outreach from the Oregon delegation, NRSC honored its commitment and released the final sum to TSWCD.

“When Oregonians make a promise, we keep it. The federal government should be held to the same standard,” said Rep. Salinas. “Tualatin Soil and Water did the work to improve our waterways, and Washington County taxpayers should never have been left holding the bag. I’m glad we got this money out the door and where it belongs.”

“Supporting threatened species and their habitats reflects Oregon values and our commitment to environmental protection, and I was grateful when the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District secured federal funds to improve fish habitat in Washington County,” said Rep. Bonamici. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration paid only about half of the promised funding, leaving Washington County taxpayers to pick up the balance. I’m glad that my colleagues and I were able to help resolve this issue and secure all the funds the water conservation district needed for the project."

“Thanks to our efforts, this funding is finally moving forward and will help ensure the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District can continue its work to improve waterways in Washington County,” said Sen. Merkley.“Oregon’s native fish are the lifeblood of our state, supporting the health and vitality of our communities, local economies, and Tribes who have been here since time immemorial. I’ll keep pushing to secure the necessary federal funds to protect our state’s ecosystems for generations to come.”

“I’m glad the full-court press by the delegation unlocked these resources promised by the federal government to the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District,” Wyden said. “These funds will keep waterways improvements on track, helping with water quality and fish habitat alike in Washington County.”

“The Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District much appreciates Congresswoman Salinas and her staff for their work in helping the District receive payment from the U.S. Department of Agriculture for a successful fish habitat project in the Gales Creek watershed of Washington County,” said Dean P. Moberg, Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District Treasurer. “We were impressed with the staff's quick understanding of the payment problem we faced, and we are grateful for the Congresswoman's exceptional response. The letter Congresswoman Salinas provided, along with Congresswoman Bonamici and Senators Merkley and Wyden, was surely instrumental in cutting through red tape and securing the payment of over one half million dollars in federal assistance that had been held up for this project. This payment will greatly facilitate the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District's work in helping residents of Washington County conserve natural resources with voluntary and locally led projects.

title: Peters Urges Trump Admin to Cancel Mass Deportation Flights to Afghanistan and Iran
text:
San Diego, CA. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led 65 bicameral Members of Congress on a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, demanding the immediate cancellation of any deportation flights carrying Afghans and Iranians, whether sent directly or through another country.

This letter comes after reports that over 150 Afghans could be deported to Pakistan in the coming days, which would constitute one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans ever. San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, with nearly 5,000 resettling in the region. The Members also expressed concern over another flight with a mass deportation of Iranians — the first since the U.S. launched its military conflict against Iran— and that relatives of Afghans who helped American troops could be among those on board.

“Our nation made a promise to stand by Afghans who risked their lives and their families’ safety to stand by U.S. service members,” the Members wrote, adding that deporting them “is a violation of that promise and our moral obligations to the Afghan community who stood alongside our troops.”

The Members emphasized the well-documented danger awaiting deportees. The State Department lists Afghanistan as a Level 4 “Do Not Travel” country, and for those who aided U.S. forces, “their assistance to U.S. troops puts a target on these individuals and their families to this day.” They detail the torture, detention, and extrajudicial killing of dissidents and LGBTQ persons, as well as the severe repression of women — noting that women and LGBTQ refugees could be on the flight.

The Members also raised alarm over reports that Iranians, including women, Christian converts, and pro-democracy activists, may be deported to Iran, where they face imprisonment, torture, and a possible death sentence. “Sending people who sought protection from the Islamic Republic of Iran back to a war zone and a repressive regime is unconscionable,” they wrote. They cited how even President Trump has warned about the dangers faced by pro-democracy and anti-government protesters in Iran.

The Members stressed that routing a flight through a third country does not change U.S. obligations, and urged the Trump Administration to warn Pakistan that the U.S. will not accept its participation in sending deportees onward to the Taliban.

These individuals “came to the U.S. because they believed in its promise of democracy, religious freedom, and liberty,” the Members concluded, and “we must uphold those values and commitments, not abandon people to autocratic regimes.”

“Sixty-six members of Congress, from both chambers, needed less than 24 hours to say what every veteran of the Afghanistan war already knows: you don’t hand the people who stood with our troops to the Taliban. When even the Taliban are voicing ‘serious concern’ about your deportation plan, you’ve lost the moral argument and the national security one. This flight isn’t immigration enforcement. It’s a betrayal with a boarding pass, and the whole world is watching whether America keeps its word. We are grateful to Rep. Peters for leading. Secretary Rubio and Secretary Mullin, ground this plane,” said Shawn VanDiver, U.S. Navy veteran and President and Founder of #AfghanEvac.

"Having effectively dismantled our protection system, this administration is set to deport vulnerable people back to Afghanistan and Iran, in violation of our human rights commitments and our nation's values," said Sarah Mehta, deputy director of immigration policy at the ACLU. "So many of these men and women never had a meaningful opportunity to defend their claims and are now the casualties of this administration's assault on asylum. We thank Congressman Peters for his leadership and all the members standing against these unconscionable deportations back to persecution, torture, or even death."

The Members requested an immediate response. Read the full letter here.

Background:

San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, and Rep. Peters has been a staunch advocate for the safe relocation, protection, and legal adjustment of Afghan wartime allies who served alongside U.S. forces. He is a cosponsor of the Enduring Welcome Act to codify the Office of the Coordinator for Afghan Relocation Efforts (CARE) within the State Department, and the Afghan Adjustment Act to help settle Afghans and their families who supported U.S. forces.

In September, Rep. Peters led a Congressional delegation on a letter to the Trump Administration urging them to reunite the families of U.S. service members with their loved ones stranded overseas, and to reconnect Afghans with immediate family already lawfully in the U.S. In July, he hosted a virtual town hall with Afghan allies stranded at the Camp As Sayliyah facility in Doha. And in February, Rep. Peters attended a shadow hearing where he highlighted the consequences of the Trump administration's decisions to freeze the U.S. refugee admissions program and eliminate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Afghans.

title: Reps Peters, Vargas, Levin, and Jacobs Back San Diego County Registrar of Voters Amid Trump Admin Probe for Voter Data
text:
San Diego, CA — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led members of the San Diego Congressional delegation, Reps. Juan Vargas (CA-52), Mike Levin (CA-49), and Sara Jacobs (CA-51), in a letter to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche amid the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) attempt to sanction voter rolls across California, including in San Diego County’s Registrars of Voters (ROV).

The DOJ demanded that San Diego’s ROV provide voter information for over 1,700 voters, including driver’s license numbers, Social Security numbers, and voter registration applications, within 48 hours, and withhold their ballots until their citizenship is confirmed. In its response, the County pushed back against several unsubstantiated claims and argued that the DOJ's probe violated several election laws.

The Members' letter reinforced the County’s claims and acknowledged that California’s registrars follow all state and federal election laws, including citizenship attestation and database verification through the California Secretary of State. They argued that the DOJ’s letter cites no legal authority to direct county ballot administration and that it violates the National Voter Registration Act’s (NVRA) 90-day quiet period against systematically removing voters from the rolls.

“The information requested by DOJ is intended to confirm the department’s unsubstantiated allegations of noncitizen voting in California,” the Members noted, also pointing to the data cited by DOJ, which the Agency itself conceded “may be outdated or incomplete.”

The Members also stated that unverified fraud allegations do not give registrars authority to violate federal law by refusing to count the votes of people already deemed eligible. They added that the DOJ’s demand fails to explain who would determine citizenship status, how, or when, less than a week before Election Day.

“The request from DOJ violates the NVRA, Voting Rights Act, California state law, and jeopardizes Californians’ constitutional right to vote,” the Members concluded, adding that “as Members of the California Congressional delegation, we commend the work of our state ROVs to ensure state and federal election laws are upheld.”

Background: Over the past several weeks, the DOJ has escalated pressure on California before Election Day and made unsubstantiated claims that large numbers of illegal voters are on the rolls. Federal courts have repeatedly intervened and denied the Administration’s attempt to interfere.

Lee (PA-12) joined House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) and Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) in demanding answers from the Trump Administration over its failure to adequately enforce federal transparency laws governing corporations and union-busting consultants.

In aletter to Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) Director Elisabeth Messenger, the lawmakers raised serious concerns about widespread failures by employers and anti-union consultants to disclose how much money they spend attempting to influence workers' decisions to organize.

Too often, when workers exercise their right to organize a union, corporations and bosses hire outside consultants to wage anti-union campaigns. Over the last several decades, union-avoidance has become a multi-billion-dollar industry. The latest analysis found that companies spend approximately $1.7 billion every year, including nearly $500 million on union-busting consultants, to break their organizing drives. Some consultants are reportedly paid $500 per hour or $4,000 per day for their services.

Under the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), employers and consultants are required to file public reports about their matter because it allows workers to see how much their bosses are spending to influence their decision to unionize. However, for decades, employers and union-busting consultants have routinely failed to meet this requirement, allowing bosses and their consultants to operate in the shadows. Under the Trump Administration, the problem is only becoming worse. A recent watchdog report found that, as of August 8, 2026, nearly 60 percent of employers required to file a disclosure in 2025 have still not submitted their reports—the largest year-over-year decline on record.

“Over the last several years, while worker organizing has skyrocketed, employers have increasingly responded with hostile anti-union campaigns, including by hiring well-compensated outside consultants. As more employers seek to quash their workers’ unionization drives, it is imperative that employer and consultant disclosure requirements under the LMRDA are robustly enforced by OLMS, so workers have a complete picture of who is attempting to influence their decision as they exercise their right to organize,” wrote the Members.

To determine whether OLMS is effectively carrying out its responsibility to enforce the LMRDA, the Members requested a response to their extensive questions by no later than November 16, 2026.

title: Balint, Warren, Colleagues Demand Answers from McDonald’s on Whether AI Pricing Tools are Raising Prices and Facilitating Collusion
text:
Text of Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. — Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL), a member of the House Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) demanded answers from McDonald’s President and CEO Chris Kempczinski about how the company generates AI-driven pricing recommendations, whether McDonald’s pressures franchisees to follow them, and how the company assesses the technology’s potential harm to consumers and competition. The letter came after reports that the company is using artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the “optimal price” for individual menu items at each of its locations and pushing franchisees to adopt these AI-based prices.

“We are concerned that McDonald’s may be using AI to squeeze consumers into paying higher prices, and that its AI pricing tools may facilitate collusion between franchisees who should be operating as competitors,” wrote the lawmakers.

U.S. Representatives Greg Casar (D-Texas), Jesús “Chuy” García (D-Ill.), and Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Pa.) also signed the letter.

According to recent reports, McDonald’s has developed an AI-based pricing tool that it may be using to recommend specific prices for each individual store, building off the massive trove of consumer data that Amazon has collected through its loyalty program and mobile app. For example, two McDonald’s-operated restaurants just two miles apart in Fresno, California reportedly charged prices that differed by as much as 21 percent for the same menu items. The lawmakers raised particular concerns about McDonald’s use of AI-based pricing at a time when food prices are rising nationwide and particularly at McDonald’s. One report found that certain McDonald’s menu prices doubled between 2014 and 2024, rising more than three times as fast as overall inflation and driving away customers who previously relied on McDonald’s for an affordable meal.

“We are concerned that McDonald’s is using its extensive consumer data and algorithmic pricing tools to unfairly raise prices on consumers who are already struggling with high food and dining costs,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers also questioned McDonald’s for reportedly putting pressure on franchisees to adopt its pricing recommendations, including through new business standards and potential consequences for franchise renewals. They warned that encouraging competing franchisees to rely on a shared pricing tool informed by nonpublic data could undermine independent pricing decisions and raise antitrust concerns.

“While McDonald’s asserts that using data and analytics to inform pricing is a standard business practice, pressuring competing franchisees to use a shared AI pricing tool built on nonpublic data is not a standard business practice, but rather a potential antitrust issue,” continued the lawmakers.

The lawmakers requested answers by November 16, 2026, on the data and algorithms used to generate pricing recommendations, the extent to which franchisees adopt those recommendations, the pressure McDonald’s places on franchisees to comply, and the company’s assessment of potential antitrust risks.

title: Harshbarger Applauds Historic Trump Administration Action to End Hidden PBM Fees and Increase Transparency
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger (R-TN), Vice Chair of the Subcommittee on Health of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released the following statement applauding the U.S. Department of Labor’s (DOL) final rule cracking down on hidden pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) fees. Under the rule, PBMs — the middlemen that manage prescription drug benefits — and their affiliated brokers must give employers that fund their own workers’ health plans a written breakdown of all the money they expect to make. That breakdown is due both when a contract is signed or renewed and every six months afterward. Employers also get the right to audit those numbers to make sure they are accurate:

“Where there's mystery, there's margin, and PBMs have made a fortune off both,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “As a pharmacist for decades, I've watched these shadowy middlemen pad their pockets at the expense of patients, employers, and the community pharmacies that serve them. Employers footing the bill for their workers' healthcare have been kept in the dark about how PBMs really make their money. Thanks to President Trump and Secretary Sonderling, those days are over. Employers will finally see the hidden rebates, fees, and markups PBMs pocket — and they'll have the right to audit the books. That means better deals, lower prescription drug costs, and more money back in the pockets of American workers and their families.”

“This is a win for every American worker who has ever paid too much at the pharmacy counter,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “For years, PBMs have operated in the shadows, pocketing hidden fees while workers and employers were left in the dark. Today, President Trump is delivering the transparency Americans deserve – and putting American workers first.”

“More transparency means more competition, and more competition means lower health care costs,” said Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Today’s new rule represents a significant step forward in this Administration’s all-of-government effort to take the guesswork out of shopping for health care – an effort in which Labor, CMS, and numerous other agencies and departments all have important roles to play.”

BACKGROUND:

On November 2, the U.S. Department of Labor finalized a rule of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), the federal law that governs employer-sponsored health plans. The rule requires PBMs — the middlemen that negotiate drug prices and run prescription drug benefits for health plans — to disclose to employers exactly how they get paid. It covers large employers that pay for their workers’ healthcare directly instead of buying coverage from an insurance company. It also applies to the brokers and consultants tied to PBMs. President Trump first directed the Labor Department to propose stricter transparency rules in his April 15, 2025, executive order, “Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First.”

Under the rule:

PBMs must give employers a written breakdown of all the money they expect to make from their contract — when the contract is signed or renewed, and every six months after that, or every three months if the employer asks.

For the first time, PBMs must disclose three major sources of hidden profit:

Rebates and other payments from drug companies;

The “spread,” when a PBM charges a health plan more for a drug than it pays the pharmacy and keeps the difference; and

Fees PBMs take back from pharmacies after a prescription is filled.

Employers can audit the numbers to make sure they are accurate.

The rule applies to employers with roughly 100 or more employees or plan members.

Self-insured employer health plans cover about 90 million Americans. The Labor Department projects the rule will lower prescription drug costs for plans and participants by as much as $22 billion over 10 years. The rule takes effect January 4, 2027, and applies to plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2027.

Congresswoman Harshbarger championed two bills that laid the groundwork for this rule:

PBM Reform Act: Introduced in July 2025 with Congressman Buddy Carter (R-GA), the bipartisan bill would require PBMs to give employers and patients semiannual reports on drug spending, rebates and formulary decisions, and would decouple PBM compensation from drug prices in Medicare Part D. Provisions of the bill helped shape the PBM reforms President Trump signed into law Feb. 3 as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 — the law this rule implements. That law also requires PBMs to pass 100% of manufacturer rebates and fees through to employer plans for plan years beginning on or after August 3, 2028.

PBM Sunshine and Accountability Act: Introduced in April 2023, the bill would require PBMs to report the rebates and fees they receive from drug manufacturers — including amounts they keep rather than pass through to health plans — and the payments they claw back from pharmacies, and would extend that reporting to employer group health plans. The Labor Department rule now requires PBMs to disclose many of the same categories of compensation directly to employers.

title: Representative Min and Senator Welch Demand Answers from Former Trump Attorney Alina Habba-Mildon on Influence over President’s Pardon of Corrupt Venezuelan Banker Julio Herrera Velutini
text:
Washington, DC. — U.S. Representative Dave Min (D-CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Anti-Corruption Task Force and U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on the Constitution, are demanding answers from former Senior Adviser to the Attorney General Alina Mildon on her reported role in President Trump’s decision to grant Julio Herrera Velutini—who pleaded guilty to violating U.S. campaign finance laws—a full presidential pardon. The letters come as President Trump criticized his former attorney’s $50 million agreement with Mr. Herrera as “totally obnoxious and outrageous,” and “not acceptable.”

In their letters, the lawmakers express concern that the timing of Ms. Habba-Mildon’s hiring and Mr. Herrera’s daughter’s contribution to MAGA Inc. raise questions about whether improper considerations, including quid pro quo or “pay-to-play” dynamics, may have affected President Trump’s decision to pardon him. These letters are part of a broader bicameral investigation led by Representative Min and Senator Welch into potential corruption surrounding President Trump’s decisions to grant presidential pardons.

The lawmakers write: “Article II, Section 2, Clause 1 of the U.S. Constitution authorizes the President to ‘grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offenses against the United States, except in Cases of Impeachment.’ The U.S. Supreme Court has characterized executive clemency as ‘an act of grace’ exercised for the ‘public welfare.’ President Trump’s use of this authority appears to deviate from this traditional purpose. Congress has a compelling interest in ensuring that the constitutional pardon power is exercised with fairness and transparency. Given these circumstances, we are seeking additional information to better understand the extent to which influence and access may have overridden the standard pardon review process.”

In August 2022, Mr. Herrera was criminally charged with providing $300,000 to a super political action committee (PAC) in violation of a campaign finance law barring contributions or donations by foreign nationals to U.S. federal, state, or local elections. Mr. Herrera financially supported the reelection campaign of Puerto Rico’s governor in exchange for her pledge to remove a top banking regulator who had scrutinized one of Mr. Herrera’s banks.

According to public reporting, Ms. Mildon entered into an employment agreement with Mr. Herrera’s family in late 2025, while she was serving as an adviser at the Justice Department. She also previously served as President Trump’s personal lawyer and as the Acting U.S. Attorney for New Jersey. In the hiring contract, Mr. Velutini’s family agreed to pay her $50 million over four years to be general counsel at Concord Partners, a company set up by Mr. Velutini’s daughter days before she signed the contract. Ms. Mildon finalized the deal with Concord Partners while she was still serving at the Justice Department.

Ms. Mildon then began working for Concord Partners on January 1, 2026, while serving as a senior adviser to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, overseeing U.S. attorneys. Two weeks later, Mr. Herrera received a pardon on January 15, 2026. Since President Trump’s election in November 2024, his 27-year-old daughter, a self-employed financial consultant, also donated $3.5 million to MAGA Inc., a Trump-supporting super PAC.

Read and download the lawmakers’ full letters to Alina Habba-Mildon and Julio Herrera Velutini.

In May, Senator Welch and Rep. Min sent letters to 17 individuals who received pardons or commutations under circumstances that warrant further congressional scrutiny, including several individuals connected to major fraud schemes, financial crimes, and high-profile political or financial relationships tied to President Trump and his associates. The earlier letters sought information regarding the clemency process, including whether financial contributions, lobbyists, intermediaries, or personal connections played a role in securing presidential clemency.

Among the individuals who received letters are convicted fraudsters, political fundraisers, corporate executives, and wealthy donors, such as Changpeng Zhao, whose cases have generated public reporting suggesting unusual access to Trump’s network of political allies and associates, direct lobbying efforts, large political donations, or other concerning connections surrounding their clemency requests.

The lawmakers continued their investigation in June, sending four additional letters to the Department of Justice’s Office of the Pardon Attorney, the White House Office of Records Management, the White House Pardon Czar, and the United States Secret Service. In October, the lawmakers initiated a probe into the influence of cabinet members, U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin, in Trump’s decision to pardon convicted felons.

text:

America is back!

Congratulations on your election to the 120th Congress. I write to humbly request your support in connection with my candidacy to serve as the next Speaker of the House of Representatives.

Accountability

We must root out corrupt price gouging, clean up the mess at the Supreme Court and ban Members of Congress from trading stocks. Accountability begins at home.

Anyone who is stealing from the American people, ripping off the American people or screwing over the American people can no longer hide. We are going to hold the crooks accountable.

American Values

Finally, we must restore classic American values like liberty and justice for all, equal protection under the law, the unfettered right to vote in a representative democracy and our heritage as a nation of immigrants. To that end, I look forward to drawing upon the insights and perspectives of every single part of the Caucus in the days and weeks ahead. House Democrats must deliver dramatic change.

Our hard-fought success gives us the opportunity to restore the promise of an affordable America in every community. The next chapter in our country’s 250-year journey begins today.

Thank you for your consideration of my candidacy to serve as the 57th Speaker of the United States House of Representatives.

Sincerely,

Hakeem Jeffries

Democratic Leader

title: Cambridge Day: ‘Blue wave’ makes Clark likely majority leader in House
text:
During Tuesday’s much-anticipated midterm elections, West Coast polls were just starting to close when media outlets like CNN and NBC began to project control of the U.S. House of Representatives would flip to Democrats. While final counts are still pending, eyes have already begun to turn to January’s leadership elections within the party, in which current House Minority Whip Katherine Clark is poised to become the first woman to serve as House majority leader.

Clark represents Massachusetts’ 5th Congressional District, which covers most of the western half of Cambridge and stretches from Winthrop to Framingham. She ran unopposed in this year’s general election, winning her eighth term.

Clark has held some form of elected office in Massachusetts for a quarter of a century. She launched her political career when she was elected to the Melrose School Committee in 2001, then served in the state House and Senate before claiming the U.S. House seat left vacant when then-Rep. Ed Markey ran for U.S. Senate in 2012. She climbed the ranks of House leadership, and served as assistant speaker of the House of Representatives from 2021-2023 alongside then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi (the assistant speaker role no longer exists due to a restructuring of party leadership following the 2022 midterms).

She’s not the only Democratic leader expected to make history, as Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D.-N.Y., will likely become the first Black speaker of the House.

For this year’s midterms, Clark has modeled a disciplined message focused on affordability that has been a winning recipe for Democrats in purple districts. Near-term priorities of hers include improving oversight of the Trump administration and bringing a swift end to the war with Iran.

As results showed Democrats retaining seats in districts Republicans redrew to improve their electoral prospects in states such as Florida, Clark told NPR “It’s all good news for the American people,” she said. “We are on the road to a very solid majority.”

title: WGBH: Katherine Clark poised to become first-ever woman House Majority Leader
text:
The “blue wave” of Democrats taking the majority in both chambers of Congress could make soon make Rep. Katherine Clark one of the most powerful people in Washington.

Clark, who ran uncontested in her reelection bid in District 5 and is currently the House Democratic Whip, is poised to likely become House Majority Leader. She would be the first woman to have that role.

Speaking after the Democrats’ sweeping victories, Clark talked about the stories of everyday Americans who have struggled with high costs.

“Their stories are what are going to propel us forward,” Clark said. “And we are proud of the Democrats who have won tonight. But we are so proud when we are gonna be able, on January 3, to get to work for them.”

Peter Ubertaccio, a political scientist at Stonehill College, said Clark’s chances of becoming majority leader are about as excellent as one could imagine.

“When your party is as successful as it was last night, there’s no real reason for party members to consider dispensing with their leadership,” he said.

Ubertaccio said Clark has developed a reputation around her thoughtfulness, attentiveness and organizational skills. And while it’s not automatic that Clark gets the role, he said there’s every reason to believe that Democrats will line up behind her and other party leaders after the performance in the midterm elections.

“It’s pretty rare to see popular leaders like Katherine Clark seriously challenged for [a] leadership position,” Ubertaccio said.

If she gets the role, Clark would be second to only the Speaker of the House, a role likely to be filled by current minority leader Hakeem Jeffries. Ubertaccio said the skills Clark has honed as Whip would help her, although she would be taking on a much more expansive role.

But he said the next two years will be a challenge for Democrats in both the House and Senate, with President Donald Trump already gearing up to use his veto power.

“Her challenge is twofold: Keep your caucus together and that is always a challenge … But then do so when the president is of a different party,” Ubertaccio said. “And so the compromises that you may have to make in order to get a president to not veto a bill, if that’s the goal, is going to test the allegiance of your party members.”

Erin O’Brien, political scientist at UMass Boston, said being number two in the majority party comes with much more control than being in the minority. And she pointed out that having a person in such a high-ranking position could bode well for Massachusetts.

“There’s a lot of national players in Massachusetts politics, and Katherine Clark has quietly ascended to an important role,” she said.

title: Hickenlooper & Hurd Lead Colorado Congressional Delegation in Support of Major Presidential Disaster Request for Southwestern Colorado Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper and Representative Jeff Hurd led the Colorado Congressional Delegation, including Senator Michael Bennet and U.S. Representatives Diana DeGette, Joe Neguse, Jason Crow, Lauren Boebert, Brittany Pettersen, Jeff Crank, and Gabe Evans, in a letter to President Trump expressing strong support for Governor Jared Polis’ request for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration following devastating and historic flooding and debris flows in Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley.

“We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on October 31, 2026, for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley in response to the recent extensive and devastating flooding throughout the region,” wrote the lawmakers. “While this request pertains to the initial flooding on October 22-25, we are writing in the midst of a second catastrophic flooding event across the same region, which adds urgency to this request. These impacts are compounded by the damaging flooding in October 2025, which have seriously strained available resources for recovery for previously affected communities.”

The Governor’s request seeks Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funding for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, where state and federal officials have already validated nearly $27 million in eligible damages. The flooding also impacted Alamosa, Conejos, Dolores, Hinsdale, La Plata, Mineral, Montezuma, Ouray, San Juan, and San Miguel Counties, where damage assessments continue and additional requests for federal assistance are expected.

In late October and early November, severe storms brought devastating flooding and debris flows to Southwestern Colorado, damaging roads, bridges, utilities, homes, and businesses, and cutting off access to entire communities. Preliminary assessments for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties have identified approximately $10.6 million in damage to local roads, bridges, and culverts; $2.44 million in damage to public utilities; and $8.59 million in damage to parks and recreation facilities. These figures do not include additional damage assessments underway or separate federal highway repair costs.

“Without additional support, residents could face unsafe homes and drinking water, long delays in rebuilding critical roads and bridges, and the loss of local businesses,” wrote the lawmakers. “Successful recovery is essential to restoring these communities’ economies, which depend on agriculture, tourism, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing.”

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on October 31, 2026, for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley in response to the recent extensive and devastating flooding throughout the region. While this request pertains to the initial flooding on October 22-25, we are writing in the midst of a second catastrophic flooding event across the same region, which adds urgency to this request. These impacts are compounded by the damaging flooding in October 2025, which have seriously strained available resources for recovery for previously affected communities.

Beginning October 22, 2026, torrential rain fell on the San Juan Mountains and San Luis Valley, already saturated by weeks of rainfall. During this initial flooding event, the San Juan River in Pagosa Springs crested at its second-highest level since 1911, and the Rio Grande reached approximately 11,000 cubic feet per second, surpassing its 1949 record. Although assessments are ongoing, totals showed the initial flooding damaged approximately 700 homes across Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, completely destroying 16 homes and 6 commercial buildings. The flooding caused extensive damage to multiple roads and bridges, overwhelmed wastewater systems, and contaminated private wells. The Colorado National Guard airlifted stranded residents to safety, and we are grateful that no fatalities have been reported.

As outlined in the Governor’s expedited request, the affected counties and Tribe have suffered damages severe enough to qualify for the Public Assistance (PA) Program. The Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment validated$26,989,000 in PA-eligible damages. As assessments continue, additional losses are likely to be identified with additional assistance requested. Granting the Governor’s initial request for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties will expedite urgent repairs for public infrastructure damages.

The State of Colorado is also requesting the activation of the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program for these counties in order to implement better infrastructure solutions to protect against future monsoon seasons and flood events. As these local communities have historically been proudly self-reliant, they are eager to rebuild more resiliently.

Successful recovery is essential to restoring these communities’ economies, which depend on agriculture, tourism, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. In already isolated rural areas, road closures are cutting residents off from their homes, schools, work, and essential services. We appreciate the Federal Highway Administration moving quickly to approve $6.5 million in quick release funds to help with immediate repairs on US Highway 160, US 550, and Colorado Highway 151, all which provide critical routes into the communities most impacted by this disaster. Without additional support, residents could face unsafe homes and drinking water, long delays in rebuilding critical roads and bridges, and the loss of local businesses.

We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration.

Sincerely,

###
