title: Beyer Testifies Against Trump’s Proposed Vanity Arch, Urges National Capital Planning Commission to Reject Proposal
text:
Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), testified before the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) today, urging the Commission to reject the Trump Administration’s proposed 250-foot arch on Columbia Island.

The 12-member Commission, which oversees federal construction and planning projects in the National Capital Region and is now led by Trump allies, is expected to vote on the proposed arch later this evening.

During his testimony, Beyer said:

“While the President has called for the project to be “converted” to a base for drones and snipers, that appears nowhere in this Commission’s consideration of the project. Apparently, placing a large weapons cache within feet of tourists, pedestrians, cyclists, Metro riders, and drivers commuting to work is not worth serious concern by a Commission tasked with region-wide planning.

“I can only conclude that by rubber-stamping the Arch without considering that position, this Commission is either calling the President a liar, or knowingly moving forward with an incomplete and potentially-fraudulent application.”

Beyer’s full written testimony is available here, and video of his remarks is available here.

Beyer’s remarks follow below:

“I am proud to represent Virginia’s Eighth Congressional District, home to Arlington National Cemetery and adjacent to the proposed location of this project on Columbia Island.

“In my time in Congress, I have never seen a project with such profound, widespread opposition from the very people who it will affect most.

“I therefore testify today as both the family member of parents, grandparents, and a sister buried at Arlington National Cemetery, and as another voice joining the many residents of Northern Virginia who have spoken out against this project.

“I have seen and heard their concerns, and I expect you to give them the same respect and consideration.

“To echo their sentiments, the proposed “Triumphal Arch” is a disgrace and an unnecessary danger to the area, for no other reason than to build a monument to the President’s ego.

“The evidence before you is overwhelming.

“Despite the Administration rushing this process through every step of the process, the National Park Service still found that it will harm dozens of nearby historic sites.

“That includes creating a permanent blight in the solemn viewshed of Arlington National Cemetery, turning our government’s back on the servicemembers buried there and their families.

“And erecting a 250-foot structure on a small island in the Potomac will not only affect irreplaceable historic sites.

“It will snarl traffic for years, impact the nearby airport, and present even more serious threats to public safety that this Commission has refused to acknowledge and grapple with.

“While the President has called for the project to be “converted” to a base for drones and snipers, that appears nowhere in this Commission’s consideration of the project.

“Apparently, placing a large weapons cache within feet of tourists, pedestrians, cyclists, Metro riders, and drivers commuting to work is not worth serious concern by a Commission tasked with region-wide planning.

“I can only conclude that by rubber-stamping the Arch without considering that position, this Commission is either calling the President a liar or knowingly moving forward with an incomplete and potentially-fraudulent application.

“That is only one of the many times the American people have been lied to at every step of this project.

“They have heard lies that this project was approved by Congress more than 100 years ago. It was not.

“Moving forward without Congressional authorization is a violation of Congress’s Constitutional authority, and that authorization has not been granted.

“The American people have also heard lies that the process would be transparent. It has not been.

“In September, I drove down to Columbia Island myself to find workers operating heavy equipment.

“They refused to answer whether that machinery was part of preparation for the Arch, despite a court-ordered requirement that notice be given ahead of any work.

“It’s time for the lies to stop, and for this sham process to end.

“I urge you to take your responsibilities seriously, and to resist political pressure to rubber-stamp this unjustified, harmful, and disgraceful project.”

Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.

title: Buchanan Honors Hometown Golf Champion Nelly Korda
text:
Celebrates the Accomplishments of Bradenton Native, Olympic Gold Medalist, 19-Time LPGA Tour Winner and U.S. Open Women’s Titlist Professional Women’s Golfer

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan joined the City of Bradenton for Nelly Korda Day, celebrating hometown native and professional golfer Nelly Korda. He presented her with a Congressional Record tribute honoring her achievements and an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol in her honor.

“Nelly is not only the best women’s golfer in the world but also a shining example of everything that makes our community great,” said Buchanan. “My granddaughter is a golfer and Nelly is a true inspiration to her. She, like many others across southwest Florida, watch how Nelly competes, how she handles both victory and disappointment and how she carries herself on and off the course. It means so much for young athletes to see someone from their own backyard rise to the very top of the game. Nelly has brought tremendous pride to Bradenton and our nation, and I was honored to recognize her.”

Korda is an Olympic gold medalist and 19-time LPGA Tour winner. Her four major championships include the Chevron Championship and her first U.S. Women’s Open title this year. She won the first tournament of 2026 and returned to the top of the world rankings as the number one player in women’s golf. In September she represented the United States at the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, where she and her teammate became the first pair ever to win five matches in a row together. Her 2024 season was one of the most impressive the sport has ever seen. She won seven tournaments that year, including a dramatic victory in front of a hometown crowd at the Bradenton Country Club. She was also named LPGA Tour Player of the Year.

Beyond the trophies, Korda has become a role model for young athletes across Manatee County. Young girls throughout the community now pick up a golf club believing they can become champions too, because someone from their own hometown has shown them the way.

You can read the Congressional Record HERE or below.

Mr. BUCHANAN. — Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor Nelly Korda of Bradenton, Florida, one of the greatest golfers in the world, whose achievements have filled our hometown with pride.

Nelly was born in Bradenton on July 28, 1998, into a family that loves sports. Her father, Petr, was a champion tennis player who won the Australian Open, and her mother, Regina, played tennis at the Olympic Games. Her older sister, Jessica, is also a winner on the LPGA Tour, and her younger brother, Sebastian, is a professional tennis player. The Kordas could have lived anywhere in the world, but they chose Bradenton as their home, and our community has cheered for Nelly every step of the way.

Nelly turned professional in 2016 as a teenager and quickly showed the world what Bradenton already knew. In 2021, she won her first major championship and, that same summer, stood atop the podium at the Olympic Games in Tokyo with a gold medal for the United States. In 2024, she put together one of the most impressive seasons the sport has ever seen, winning seven tournaments and being named the LPGA Tour’s Player of the Year.

Her bond with Bradenton was on full display in January 2024, when a professional tournament came to Bradenton Country Club, just down the road from the hospital where she was born. Friends, family, and neighbors lined the course to cheer her on. Late on the final day, it looked as though the title might slip away, but Nelly fought back with two brilliant shots on the closing holes and went on to win in a dramatic finish. Afterward, she thanked the hometown crowd for staying positive and carrying her to victory. For one unforgettable week, the golf world turned its attention to our city, and Bradenton’s own daughter delivered.

Like every great athlete, Nelly has faced setbacks. In 2025, she went the entire season without a win. Rather than be discouraged, she went back to work, and in 2026 she came back stronger than ever. She won the very first tournament of the year and finished first or second in each of her first six events, something only one other woman in history had ever done. She went on to win the Chevron Championship and the U.S. Women’s Open, two of the most important events in women’s golf, and returned to her place as the number one player in the world. In September, she once again wore the colors of the United States at the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, where she and her teammate made history as the first pair ever to win five matches in a row together.

Yet Nelly’s greatest gift to Bradenton may be the example she sets. Across Manatee County, young girls now pick up a golf club believing they, too, can become champions, because someone from their own hometown has shown them the way. Parents point to her as a model of hard work and perseverance, and whenever Nelly’s name appears in headlines around the world, the name of Bradenton travels right alongside it.

This tribute is personal for me as well. My own granddaughter is a golfer, and a very good one. Like so many young players in our community, she considers Nelly a true inspiration. She watches how Nelly competes, how she handles both victory and disappointment, and how she carries herself on and off the course. I have seen firsthand how much it means to a young athlete to watch someone from her own backyard rise to the very top of the game.

Through it all, Nelly has remained humble and gracious. She is quick to credit her family, her team, and the people who have supported her since she was a little girl. She represents the very best of our community: talent matched with determination, success matched with kindness, and a deep love for the place she calls home.

Mr. Speaker, on behalf of the people of Florida’s 16th Congressional District, I ask my colleagues to join me in congratulating Nelly Korda on her extraordinary achievements, in thanking her for the honor she has brought to the City of Bradenton and to our nation, and in wishing her many more years of success.

title: Reps. Chu, Moore Reintroduce EITC Age Parity Act to Expand Tax Credit to Younger and Older Workers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Gwen Moore (WI-04) reintroduced the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Age Parity Act, which would eliminate age restrictions that currently prevent millions of young and older workers without children from claiming the EITC.

The EITC is one of our nation’s most effective anti-poverty tools. In 2024, it lifted 4.4 million people above the poverty line, including over two million children, and reduced the severity of poverty for more than 16 million Americans. But the credit excludes a crucial segment of the workforce. Unless you have a qualifying child, the EITC is only available to those between ages 25 and 64, leaving millions of younger and older works ineligible solely because of their age. The EITC Age Parity Act would solve this issue by eliminating the EITC’s upper age limit and expanding eligibility to workers as young as 18.

“The EITC is one of the most impactful and transformative anti-poverty tools we have at our disposal. Unfortunately, arbitrary age limits exclude millions of hardworking Americans who could benefit from it greatly,” said Rep. Chu. “Right now, a 23-year-old stocking shelves and a 66-year-old still working to make ends meet, neither with children at home, are shut out of the EITC for no reason other than their age. I’m proud to reintroduce the EITC Age Parity Act with Rep. Moore to lift more families out of poverty and put more money back in the pockets of millions of workers.”

“At a time when American families and workers are struggling with higher costs for just about everything, our tax laws should not be taxing workers into poverty. That is why I have long championed updates to the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), one of our nation’s largest anti-poverty tools. While the American Rescue Plan Act made important changes to the EITC, including allowing younger and older adults without children to benefit from this refundable credit, those temporary changes expired, depriving some of our most vulnerable workers of critical assistance. The EITC Age Parity Act would permanently allow younger and older workers to benefit from the EITC, a crucial first step in ensuring that our tax code can better serve all our workers,” said Rep. Moore.

“We applaud the leadership of Rep. Chu and Rep. Moore on behalf of the EITC Age Parity Act to permanently eliminate age restrictions that prevent young and older workers from claiming the EITC,” said Amy Everitt, President of Golden State Opportunity. “This invaluable tax credit boosts workforce participation and sparks local economic growth. Yet, we need to make sure our policies better serve the workers who have been left behind by our best policies. With the cost of living rising, every worker needs every dollar they have already earned.”

The bill is cosponsored by Reps. Gwen Moore (WI-04), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-At Large), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), and Valerie Foushee (NC-04).

The bill is endorsed by Golden State Opportunity (GSO).

title: Lone Star in the Capital: Doggett, Daughters of the Republic of Texas Unveil Base of Republic of Texas Legation Memorial
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Fish and Wildlife and Parks Kevin Lilly, a fellow Texan, and the Elisabet Ney Chapter of the Daughters of the Republic of Texas unveiled the Lone Star base of the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial at 630 Indiana Avenue NW, adjacent to its intersection with Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C. The memorial was approved by Congress in legislation authored by Doggett, the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial Act. It memorializes the Texans who worked for almost a decade to negotiate the admission of Texas into the United States as the 28th state.

Congressman Lloyd Doggett (fourth from right) with Assistant Secretary of the Interior Kevin Lilly, Priscilla Roberts, Kitty Hoeck, Grace Boatright, members of the Elisabet Ney Chapter of the Daughters of the Republic of Texas and National Park Service staff at the ceremony marking the start of construction of the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial on Indiana Avenue NW, November 5, 2026.

The Lone Star base, a five-pointed star of white Mount Airy granite, sits in an existing granite planter on the 600 block of Indiana Avenue NW, steps from the U.S. Navy Memorial. Today’s unveiling marks the start of construction of the memorial. The site sits among five of the eight places where, according to research by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, the Legation’s diplomats lived and worked out of boarding houses and hotels, including the site of today’s Navy Memorial, where Texas Minister Memucan Hunt resided in 1837 and 1838.

“As a native Texan with more pride in our State after the recent election than ever before, I am pleased that this new monument recognizes an important part of our Texas heritage," said Congressman Doggett. “For almost a decade, eight different Texans conducted negotiations for the admission of Texas into the United States as the 28th state. This will likely become another point of interest especially for Texas visitors to our capital.”

“When tourists come to our Nation’s capital, they are likely unaware of an important piece of Texas lore that hides in plain sight: the lost landmarks of the Republic of Texas Legation in Washington,” he continued. “Its diplomats were sent on the very long and difficult journey from Texas to Washington, and Americans traveling in Europe can find plaques in both London and Paris that commemorate the Texas Legation. Washington had not followed suit. Most appropriately, this work has been spearheaded by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, our State’s oldest patriotic women’s organization, and Kitty Hoeck has led the way, proving that one person can make a difference with their tenacity and determination.”

“The history of the Texas Legation did not end with the annexation of Texas in 1845. Today, it lives on through the strength of the multicultural and multilingual communities that make our Lone Star State so dynamic,” shared the Congressman. “With this memorial, all those who visit our Nation’s Capital will have the opportunity to learn about this turning point in our Nation’s history and reflect on the sacrifices made by the brave diplomats who made it possible. Because Texas history is America’s history.”

About the memorial

Modest in scale, the memorial will rise from the Lone Star base unveiled today: a five-sided plinth of white granite topped by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas medallion and engraved with the story of the Texas Legation, a map of the Republic of Texas and the names of the eight diplomats the Republic sent to Washington. Plantings native to Texas and the Mid-Atlantic will surround a single sweetbay magnolia, representing the Lone Star State. The site is federal land under the National Park Service.

Background

From 1836 to 1845, the Republic of Texas kept a diplomatic legation in Washington, working first for U.S. recognition and then for annexation; Texas became the 28th state on December 29, 1845. Doggett introduced the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial Act (H.R. 3349) in June 2019. It passed the House and Senate with bipartisan support and was signed into law on December 22, 2020. The Daughters then won final approval of the site and design from the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts and the National Capital Planning Commission in 2025 and raised the full cost privately; the law bars federal funds to build the memorial.

title: Rep. Foster Unveils Discussion Draft of Legislation to Modernize Financial Regulatory Reporting and Strengthen Oversight of the Financial System
text:
Financial services driven by artificial intelligence and round-the-clock payments systems may contribute to and rapidly spread financial stress. As the financial system accelerates, real-time information and automated tools can help institutions and regulators respond faster, improve access to liquidity, and better prepare for orderly bank resolutions. Meanwhile, advances in AI are creating new cybersecurity threats. Through enhanced collective maintenance and security built in from the start, open-source software can provide stronger protection against cyber threats. Model open-source software also has the potential to lower development and reporting costs for community banks and credit unions and expand their access to advanced risk-management capabilities.

The Real-Time Regulatory Study Act directs the Federal Reserve Board, in coordination with other financial regulators, to develop, test, and publicly release open-source demonstration software to evaluate how technology can streamline regulatory obligations, reduce compliance costs, and provide regulators with real-time information on the condition of financial institutions nationwide. The Federal Reserve would seek technical contributions from financial institutions, technology providers, open-source organizations, and researchers.

title: Rep. Grijalva Reacts to Discovery of Ancestral Remains at Organ Pipe Amid Border Wall Construction
text:
Rep. Grijalva is preparing legislation to repeal DHS’ waiver authority and void existing waivers that bypass protections for Tribal sovereignty, sacred sites, and ancestral lands.

Tucson, Arizona — Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the below statement following reports about the discovery of Native American ancestral remains at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in Arizona, where border wall contractors have bulldozed through ancestral lands, disturbed native vegetation and unearthed human remains.

“This is an outrage. For months, Tribal leaders and elders have warned DHS about the devastating consequences of bulldozing through their ancestral lands, beginning with the destruction of the Las Playas Intaglio. For months, those warnings have fallen on deaf ears. Now, we are seeing exactly what they feared: sacred sites destroyed and burial grounds desecrated.

This is precisely why we must end DHS’ sweeping authority to waive laws designed to protect Tribal sovereignty, sacred sites, and environmentally sensitive lands. I will be introducing legislation to repeal that authority and void existing waivers that have allowed DHS to ignore these protections and carelessly bulldoze through much of our southern border.”

The discovery is the latest in a series of devastating impacts to culturally and historically significant sites along the southern border. title: Moore, Chu Reintroduce EITC Age Parity Act to Expand Tax Credit to Younger and Older Workers
text:
Representative Gwen Moore (WI-04) and Representative Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Age Parity Act to eliminate a barrier preventing younger and older workers without children from accessing the EITC.

Last year, 24 million workers and families received the credit, pulling millions out of poverty. But under current law, workers under the age of 25 and over the age of 65 without children are not eligible for the credit. The EITC Age Parity Act expands this credit’s eligibility so these workers can finally receive permanent support.

“At a time when American families and workers are struggling with higher costs for just about everything, our tax laws should not be taxing workers into poverty. That is why I have long championed updates to the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), one of our nation’s largest anti-poverty tools. While the American Rescue Plan Act made important changes to the EITC, including allowing younger and older adults without children to benefit from this refundable credit, those temporary changes expired, depriving some of our most vulnerable workers of critical assistance. The EITC Age Parity Act would permanently allow younger and older workers to benefit from the EITC, a crucial first step in ensuring that our tax code can better serve all our workers,” said Rep. Moore.

“The EITC is one of the most impactful and transformative anti-poverty tools we have at our disposal. Unfortunately, arbitrary age limits exclude millions of hardworking Americans who could benefit from it greatly,” said Rep. Chu. “Right now, a 23-year-old stocking shelves and a 66-year-old still working to make ends meet, neither with children at home, are shut out of the EITC for no reason other than their age. I’m proud to reintroduce the EITC Age Parity Act with Rep. Moore to lift more families out of poverty and put more money back in the pockets of millions of workers.”

title: CBS: Katherine Clark of Massachusetts will be first woman to serve as House majority leader, Hakeem Jeffries says
text:
Massachusetts Congresswoman Katherine Clark is set to make history as the first woman to become a majority leader in Congress, the leader of the House Democrats said Wednesday.

Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, widely expected to be elected the next speaker of the House after Democrats won big in the 2026 midterm elections, introduced Clark at a news conference as “the next majority leader of the House of Representatives” and “someone who will be the first woman to ever serve in that position in our 250-year journey.”

Clark, the current House minority whip who lives in Revere, was elected to Congress in 2013 to replace now-Sen. Ed Markey. The 63-year-old said she was proud to “make history” as part of the new majority.

“In the words of the great Dolly Parton, it’s been a long hard fight, but I see a brand new day a-dawning,” Clark said.

Clark has been outspoken about childcare issues, introducing the Babies Act in 2022 to support new mothers with more access to birth centers and midwives. She also bashed President Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” last year, calling it “incredibly cruel” for making cuts to Medicaid and food stamps.

Clark still needs to be elected by her House colleagues to become majority leader in the new Congress. She said Wednesday that Americans are trusting her party to do more than just “damage control” on the Trump administration.

“They have entrusted a Democratic Congress to lead us forward to something better, to make their lives easier,” she said.

Clark on Thursday officially declared her intent to run for majority leader in a letter to other Democratic representatives.

“My priority will be ensuring that every corner of our Caucus is heard and empowered to have a role in the policymaking process,” Clark wrote. “At every decision point, I intend to work closely with you to understand the needs of your district and maximize your ability to deliver for your constituents.”

Steve Kerrigan, chair of the Massachusetts Democratic Party, has known Clark since she first ran to be on the Melrose School Committee back in 2001.

“It’s huge. The last time we’ve had someone at that height in House leadership was Tip O’Neill and that was decades ago,” Kerrigan said. “I am excited for the world to get to know the really incredibly special person she is and the great leader that she is.”

WBZ-TV political analyst Jon Keller said Clark as majority leader could mean millions of dollars in funding for Massachusetts.

“That’s an area where during the last two years of the Trump administration we have really been hurt by cuts and federal research grants and other funding sources,” Keller said.

Congresswoman Clark’s office did not return WBZ’s request for an interview.

title: Kennedy Announces Nearly $150,000 in Federal Grants for Buffalo Naval Park to Tell the Stories of African American Sailors and Honor Western New York Veterans
text:
National Park Service Grant will Fund an Exhibit on African American Naval Service - Institute of Museum of Library Services Grant Supports a Virtual Wall of Honor

BUFFALO, N.Y. - Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) today announced two federal grants totaling nearly $150,000 for the Buffalo and Erie County Naval & Military Park. The National Park Service (NPS) awarded $97,176 through its African American Civil Rights Preservation and History Grants program for an African American Naval Service exhibit, which will interpret the history of racial segregation aboard the park’s historic naval vessels and the experiences of the African American sailors who served during that era. The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) awarded a $51,591 matching grant through its Inspire! Grants for Small Museums program to create a Virtual Wall of Honor that preserves and shares the stories and service records of Western New York veterans.

“The Buffalo Naval Park is where Western New York comes to remember those who served, and these grants will help it tell even more of that story,” said Congressman Kennedy. “African American sailors served our country with honor and distinction while facing segregation aboard the very ships that visitors tour today, and an honest account of their experiences belongs in our understanding of that complex history. The Virtual Wall of Honor will make it easier for families to find and learn about the veterans they love. I congratulate everyone at the Naval Park on earning these highly sought after awards and I’m glad to see this support coming to Buffalo’s waterfront.”

“These federal investments will help us preserve more than history,” said Brian Luallen, President & CEO, Buffalo Naval Park. “They will help us tell the stories of the men and women who lived it. From the experiences of African American sailors aboard our historic ships to the legacies of Western New York veterans honored on our Wall of Honor, every name represents a life and every story deserves to be told. We're grateful to Congressman Kennedy, the National Park Service, and the Institute of Museum and Library Services for helping us carry these stories forward for generations to come.”

The NPS grant is one of 54 projects in 18 states funded this year through the African American Civil Rights Preservation and History program, which draws on the Historic Preservation Fund. The IMLS grant was highly competitive. The agency received 299 applications requesting more than $11 million and made 88 awards totaling $3.3 million. In 2025, Kennedy fought back against efforts to dismantle the IMLS. The Virtual Wall of Honor will give visitors a multisensory way to explore veterans’ stories and learn about family members, hometown neighbors, and others connected to them, and the project includes staff training. Located at Canalside, the park is home to the USS The Sullivans, USS Little Rock, USS Croaker, and PTF 17. The park first opened to the public in 1979.

title: Local Leaders, Caltrain, Mullin Secure $90 Million Grant for Burlingame Grade Separation Project
text:
San Mateo, CA — U.S. Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) is pleased to share that the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) has awarded $90.4 million for construction of the Caltrain Broadway Grade Separation Project in Burlingame through the Railroad Crossing Elimination Program.

Rep. Mullin advocated in support of Caltrain’s application for the capital grant in partnership with the San Mateo County Transportation Authority (SMCTA) and the city of Burlingame. The California Public Utilities Commission ranks the Broadway crossing as the top-priority grade separation in California. More than 30,000 vehicles travel through the crossing each day. By separating the rail line from the street, the project will improve safety, reduce congestion and lower emissions.

In addition to the $90 million federal grant made possible through the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, earlier this year Rep. Mullin was able to secure an additional $3 million in federal funds for the project as part of the annual appropriations process.

“Caltrain, the City of Burlingame, and the San Mateo County Transportation Authority have been working tirelessly to make important safety upgrades at Broadway, which has been deemed the most dangerous rail crossing in all of California,” said Rep. Mullin. “I have been partnering with Caltrain, the SMCTA and the City to bring home more federal support for the Broadway Burlingame Grade Separation project and am thrilled it has rightfully earned an additional $90 million grant from the Federal Railroad Administration. In addition to the $3 million in federal Community Project Funding I brought home earlier this year, this FRA grant will go a long way to helping improve safety in our community.”

“These federal awards advance the grade separations our communities need to enhance protection for pedestrians, cyclists, drivers and our passengers, and create a safer corridor for generations to come,” said Rico E. Medina, Caltrain Board Chair.

“This federal investment marks a major milestone for the Broadway Grade Separation Project and reflects the sustained partnership among SMCTA, Caltrain, the City of Burlingame and our state and federal leaders,” said Julia Mates, chair of the San Mateo County Transportation Authority Board of Directors. “SMCTA’s local investment helped position this critical project for delivery, improving safety and regional mobility.”

“The City of Burlingame thanks its federal partners for joining our State, County and City financing team to finally make Broadway grade separation a reality,” said Burlingame Mayor Michael Brownrigg. “Hard work, sharp pencils, and leaders who focus on the long term are what helped get this critical project over the goal line, and our residents and our region will be the better and safer for it.

This FRA grant secures a critical piece of the grade separation project’s funding and keeps the project on track for construction. The partners will continue to pursue funding for additional pedestrian and bicycle circulation improvements and coordinate those improvements with project delivery. Site preparation, utility relocation and other early construction work are expected to begin in May 2027. Construction is expected to be complete in January 2032.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Expose Microplastics Hidden in Clothing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Nov. 5, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace introduced the Clothing Microplastic Transparency Act of 2026, legislation requiring clothing companies to disclose microplastic content in the products they sell.

“Americans deserve to know what is in the clothing touching their skin all day long,” said Congresswoman Mace. “While current labels list fiber content, they do not disclose microplastics. Our bill puts the facts on the tag. At a time when microplastics and other components have fueled health concerns, you deserve to know what you wear.”

The Clothing Microplastic Transparency Act would:

Require any company selling or offering clothing for sale to disclose the estimated mass of microplastic in each item through a stamp, tag, label, or similar identification.

Direct the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), in consultation with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), to issue regulations within one year of enactment, including a standardized test method companies must use to estimate microplastic content.

Treat violations as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act, enforced by the FTC.

title: Rep. Joe Neguse Announces Candidacy for Assistant Speaker
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse announced his candidacy for the position of Assistant Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. Neguse currently serves as Assistant Democratic Leader, and at Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries’ request, served as Chair of House Democrats’ Litigation Task Force in the 119th Congress.

If elected, Neguse will become the youngest lawmaker in the history of the Congress to assume the role of Assistant Speaker, a position previously held by leading voices in the Democratic Party, including Whip Katherine Clark and Senator Ben Ray Luján.

In a letter sent to his colleagues, Neguse cited efforts to ensure voices from across the House Democratic Caucus are uplifted, included, and heard. He pointed to the broad constituency of his own large congressional district in the Rocky Mountain West—spanning rural, suburban, and urban areas—as a demonstration of this ability. The millennial Congressman, 42, is the only non-coastal member of senior House Democratic leadership, and the youngest member of the team.

Neguse also highlighted his team’s work to expand support for Members, specifically by assisting new Members with their transition to Congress, enhancing staff assistance programs, and assessing and addressing the needs of congressional offices across the country. He also pointed to his successful efforts as Chair of the Litigation Task Force as an example of how he would continue to use his leadership skills to assist Committee leaders and fellow Members in fighting back against the Trump administration’s rampant lawlessness.

During the 119th Congress, the Litigation Task Force was responsible for taking unprecedented steps to stand up for the American people, filing dozens of legal challenges in federal courts across the country and paving the way for judges to strike down disastrous and unconstitutional directives from the Trump White House, including illegal tariffs, restrictions on voting by mail, stripping individuals born on U.S. soil of the guarantee to birthright citizenship, and unlawful impoundments of taxpayer funds.

Read Neguse’s entire letter to his colleagues HERE and below.

November 5, 2026

Dear Colleague:

It has been an honor to serve as Assistant Democratic Leader, and to work alongside each of you during the 119th Congress. I remain deeply inspired by the talent, commitment, and tenacity our caucus has consistently shown. With our decisive and overwhelming victory this week, it is more important than ever for the House Democratic Caucus to be unified in the 120th Congress, and to repay the faith that the American people have put in us to lower costs, end corruption, and deliver for working families. To that end, and as we embark on that road together, I write to respectfully request your support for Assistant Speaker.

I’m deeply grateful to have had the opportunity to serve our caucus in House Leadership, mostly recently as Assistant Democratic Leader and previously as a Co-Chair and Chairman of the DPCC, DCCC Recruitment/Red-to-Blue Co-Chair and National Finance Co-Chair. In each position, I’ve worked to engage everyone in our caucus, firmly rooted in my belief that every member has much to offer to the House and to the country. As someone who represents a large rural, suburban, and urban district (with agricultural communities extending all the way to the Wyoming border), I’ve long worked hard to effectively serve a broad constituency — and I’ve adopted that same approach as a member of the leadership team, ensuring voices from across our caucus and the ideological spectrum are elevated, included, and heard.

As Assistant Leader, my focus has been on serving our caucus — by expanding opportunities for members, enhancing staff assistance programs, and ensuring our office is addressing your technical needs. With your help, we launched the successful New-Member ADL Mentorship Program to assist new members with their transition to the Congress. We also worked to uplift each and every member of the broader caucus, including through monthly ADL press conferences and corresponding special order programming — elevating your talents and expertise for the benefit of the country. And through our office’s management of House Democrats’ District Director Services Program, our team has worked to assist your District staff with their everyday needs, including via our weekly roundtables, technical assistance programs, annual Conference & Fly-In, and the new District Director Mentoring program we launched earlier this year.

Finally, at the request of Leader Jeffries, I was proud to serve as Chair of the Litigation Task Force for House Democrats, and in so doing, provide Members with opportunities to weigh-in on over twenty lawsuits against the Trump Administration's lawlessness. From our successful amicus briefs in multiple cases, our groundbreaking lawsuit against ICE, and regular programming opportunities for member engagement with legal experts, I’m deeply grateful to the many members of our caucus who made the Task Force’s work so consequential and impactful. And with your support, I would be honored to continue that work with each of you and our talented Committee leaders in the 120th Congress.

If elected Assistant Speaker, my goals would be straight-forward — to prioritize direct member services for every member of our diverse and talented caucus, and to assist Speaker Jeffries and our incredible Democratic Leadership team. In addition to continuing the existing programming of the Assistant Leader’s Office, I’d relish the opportunity to launch multiple new programs, including expanding training programs for our District Directors, launching a new technical assistance program for subcommittee chairs, and enhancing the mentorship and transition programming for new members. All in all, I believe such efforts will ensure that every member and their office has the resources they need to succeed.

In sum, it has been such a privilege to work alongside each of you over the past several years, and it would truly be an honor to serve our caucus, the Congress and the country as Assistant Speaker. I look forward to continuing the conversation with you about my candidacy and ideas, and thank you so much for your consideration.

Sincerely,

title: Pelosi Statement on the Sentencing of Joshua Wong

title: Reps. Salinas, Mackenzie Introduce Bill to Protect Patients When Insurance Companies Drop Their Providers
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Rep. Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07) introduced the Right to Re-Enroll Act. The bipartisan bill would protect patients from unexpected changes to their health insurance coverage. It would allow Americans enrolled in Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace plans to switch insurance plans outside of the annual open enrollment period if their provider or health system is dropped from their insurance network.

When providers and insurance companies fail to reach agreements on contracts, patients can suddenly lose access to the clinicians and hospitals they rely on. These disputes are becoming increasingly common. Between 2021 and 2025, nearly one in five non-federal hospitals experienced a public contract dispute with an insurance company, and nearly 10 percent temporarily fell out of network with an insurer.

“Families are already paying too much for health care. They shouldn't have to worry about losing their provider on top of it,” said Rep. Salinas. “Right now, patients can find themselves stuck paying for a plan that no longer covers their provider or hospital. That's especially concerning for people living in rural areas who are far from other providers, or for people undergoing treatment who can't afford an interruption in care. No one should lose access to their provider because their insurance company and health system can't agree on a contract. This bill gives patients the freedom to find a plan that meets their needs and protects them from unexpectedly losing access to care.”

“Patients and families across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos should not have to worry about losing access to their trusted doctors or facing unexpected disruptions in care because of changes to their insurance network,” said Congressman Ryan Mackenzie. “The bipartisan Right to Re-Enroll Act would give patients more options when unexpected changes to their insurance coverage disrupt their access to care. By working across the aisle, we can put patients first and help ensure greater access to quality, affordable health care.”

Currently, Medicare Advantage enrollees have the ability to change plans when significant changes are made to their provider networks. However, Americans who purchase health insurance through ACA marketplaces do not have the same protections when their insurance company drops a provider from its network.

The Right to Re-Enroll Act would:

Give patients the right to switch plans: Create a 60-day special enrollment period for individuals enrolled in ACA marketplace plans when a provider leaves their insurance network, outside of the annual enrollment period.

Protect patients from unexpected costs: Require insurers to maintain existing coverage terms and in-network cost-sharing for qualifying patients who continue receiving care from an affected provider for 90 days.

Require insurers to notify patients: Ensure patients receive notice within seven days of a network change, including information about their right to switch plans and how changing plans could affect their deductible and out-of-pocket costs.

The legislation would apply to ACA marketplace plans beginning in 2027.

“When changes happen in insurance networks or coverage, continuity of care keeps treatment for patients safe and consistent,” said Becky Hultberg, president and CEO of the Hospital Association of Oregon. “Reducing avoidable disruption is the right thing to do for patients, safeguarding their care and easing their burden during treatment. Rep. Salinas’ Right to Re-Enroll Act puts patients first, giving them the peace of mind of knowing they can choose a different health plan during a special re-enrollment period so they can continue getting the care they need without interruption.”

This legislation is endorsed by Families USA, American Psychological Association, Young Invincibles, and the Hospital Association of Oregon.

title: Spartz Demands Sweeping Investigation into Utility Surcharges, No-Bid Contracts, Corporate Subsidies, Grid Reliability, and Eminent Domain Uses
text:
NOBLESVILLE, IN — Congresswoman Victoria Spartz (IN-05) is calling for sweeping federal and state investigations into utility surcharges, corporate subsidies, energy infrastructure costs, threats to grid reliability, and the use of eminent domain for projects benefiting private corporations.

In three letters to the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and Department of Energy (DOE), and Indiana’s new legislative leadership, Spartz is demanding independent audits, stronger property rights, greater transparency, and meaningful regulatory reforms.

“Americans are being forced to bankroll a system where powerful utilities collect guaranteed returns, wealthy corporations receive massive subsidies, and hardworking families and small businesses get stuck with higher bills,” said Rep. Spartz. “It is time to follow the money and expose who approved these sweetheart deals, who profited, and who got stuck with the bill.”

Spartz is demanding action on:

Utility surcharges, no-bid contracts, and corporate subsidies: Audit previously approved federal and state utility surcharges, special rate riders, guaranteed returns, no-bid contracts and preferential transmission development rights, tax breaks, and corporate incentives to determine whether costs were justified or improperly passed on to consumers.

Eminent domain and property rights: Reform laws allowing private property to be taken for transmission projects primarily benefiting corporate interests. Require proof of genuine public necessity, independent review of alternatives, and fair treatment of affected landowners.

Cost shifting: Require data centers and other major electricity users to pay their full generation, transmission, and infrastructure costs rather than shifting them onto families and small businesses.

Grid reliability and blackouts: Examine whether rapidly expanding electricity demand, premature power plant retirements, and delays in new generation and transmission threaten reliable electricity supplies. Develop a concrete plan for dependable natural gas and nuclear generation.

Energy costs and environmental risks: Investigate the full costs and potential pollution risks of solar, wind, and battery storage projects, including their effects on utility bills and grid reliability.

Regulatory failures: Investigate PJM and MISO governance, utility conflicts of interest, regulatory compliance failures, and national security concerns. Reform the structure, transparency, and accountability of Indiana’s Utility Regulatory Commission.

Farmland, water, and public safety: Protect productive farmland and water resources, investigate publicly subsidized infrastructure, and examine the safety of battery storage facilities proposed in flood-prone areas.

Transparency and accountability: Require independent verification of electricity demand, competitive transmission development, disclosure of financial beneficiaries, and enforceable protections against abandoned projects and stranded costs.

“We are shutting down reliable power plants while rushing to approve massive new electricity loads without adequate generation. Who is planning for the blackouts? Who is paying for the infrastructure? And who is holding these regulators accountable?” Spartz continued.

“Eminent domain must serve genuine public necessity—not become a tool for wealthy corporations to seize farmland and force families to subsidize their private developments.”

Spartz is requesting a comprehensive GAO investigation of historical utility charges and corporate incentives, federal regulatory action on large-load projects and grid reliability, and legislative reforms by Indiana’s General Assembly when it reconvenes in January.

“Indiana families should not be subsidizing billionaires’ data centers through hidden utility charges and government handouts. We need a full accounting of every dollar, independent audits, and recovery of any improper payments.”

“This is corporate welfare on the backs of American taxpayers and ratepayers. Enough is enough. Government must stop protecting powerful special interests and start protecting the people who pay the bills.”

The three letters address:

GAO: Independent investigation and audits of utility surcharges, subsidies, infrastructure costs, regulatory failures, and potential improper cost recovery. See letter HERE.

FERC and DOE: Federal action on large-load developments, grid reliability, transmission competition, generation planning, and regional grid governance. See letter HERE.

title: Rep. Sykes Announces Nearly $5,000 Federal Grant to Preserve Hudson’s 1845 Herbarium
text:
HUDSON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Hudson Library & Historical Society has been awarded $4,999 in federal Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) Library Services and Technology Act funds by the State Library of Ohio. The funds will be used to conserve an herbarium created in 1845 by Mary Strong, founder of the Hudson Female Seminary.

Strong’s herbarium is a single leather volume containing a wide variety of dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on paper, including leaves, plants, flowers, fungi, and moss. The collection offers insight into Ohio’s natural history and a window into the role female education played in Hudson’s early history.

“Our libraries and historical societies are where our community’s story is kept, and Mary Strong’s herbarium is a remarkable piece of that story,” said Rep. Sykes. “It captures Ohio’s natural history and honors the role of women’s education in Hudson’s early days. I’m proud that federal dollars are helping preserve it, and I commend the Hudson Library & Historical Society for its work to protect this treasure for future generations.”

The grant is one of 10 awarded statewide, totaling $48,627 in federal IMLS Library Services and Technology Act funds. Conservation and Preservation Grants enable libraries to conserve a single item or preserve a small, discrete group of items within their collections. Funds are used primarily to contract a professional conservator or conservation lab to ensure the materials are preserved according to best practices.

title: Rep. Dina Titus Asks Republican Leadership to Fast-Track FAIR BET Act
text:
Congresswoman Dina Titus sent a letter to House Republican leadership today urging it to include in “must-pass” legislation her measure to restore the 100 percent gambling loss deduction when the House reconvenes next week.

“Enactment of this bipartisan provision would correct an unfair change in the tax code and provide needed certainty to taxpayers, businesses, and regulated gaming markets across the country,” Congresswoman Titus wrote in the letter to House Speaker Mike Johnson and Majority Leader Steve Scalise.

A provision added to the Senate-amended version of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed by Congress last year reduced the gambling loss deduction from 100 to 90 percent. In effect, the change requires gambler to pay taxes on money they did not earn. On July 7, 2025, Congresswoman Titus introduced the FAIR BET Act, H.R.4304, to reverse the change. The legislation passed out of the House Ways and Means Committee by a vote of 38-5 in September and is awaiting action by House leadership to bring it to a floor vote.

“As Congress returns from recess and turns to end-of-year legislation, I respectfully urge Leadership to expeditiously bring a gambling loss deduction fix to the House floor and include it in a must-pass legislative vehicle,” Congresswoman Titus said.

She said the 90 percent deduction “unfairly burdens professional gamblers and casual players alike and will inevitably drive players toward offshore and unregulated markets where consumer protections are nonexistent, thereby undermining responsible gaming efforts nationwide. This will further reduce tax revenue and stifle investment by the industry here at home, costing jobs and impacting ancillary businesses.”

title: Hickenlooper, Bennet, Hurd Tour Flooding in San Luis Valley
text:
GUADALUPE – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper and Michael Bennet and Representative Jeff Hurd toured flood-damaged areas of the San Luis Valley. The lawmakers made stops in Guadalupe and South Fork to survey extensive damage to homes, businesses, and infrastructure and hear directly from local leaders about ongoing recovery needs.

The visit follows a letter sent Wednesday by the lawmakers and the entire Colorado congressional delegation urging President Trump to swiftly approve Governor Jared Polis’ request for an expedited Major Disaster Declaration following historic flooding and debris flows across Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley.

Watch Hickenlooper’s Video From South Fork, CO

“The damage we saw today is almost hard to fathom. Many of these same communities are still reeling from last fall’s floods, and now they’ve been hit again,” said Hickenlooper. “We’re grateful to the emergency management teams and first responders who are keeping people safe. We’ve also been checking in with leaders across the Southwest region to understand their recovery needs. We’ll do everything we can to coordinate with the State and our federal partners to ensure these communities get the resources they deserve as quickly as possible.”

The Governor’s request seeks Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funding for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, where state and federal officials have already validated nearly $27 million in eligible damages. The flooding also impacted Alamosa, Conejos, Dolores, Hinsdale, La Plata, Mineral, Montezuma, Ouray, San Juan, and San Miguel Counties, where damage assessments continue and additional requests for federal assistance are expected.

In late October and early November, severe storms brought devastating flooding and debris flows to Southwestern Colorado, damaging roads, bridges, utilities, homes, and businesses, and cutting off access to entire communities. Preliminary assessments for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties have identified approximately $10.6 million in damage to local roads, bridges, and culverts; $2.44 million in damage to public utilities; and $8.59 million in damage to parks and recreation facilities. These figures do not include additional damage assessments underway or separate federal highway repair costs.
